summary: Work with sprites, character sets, songs and other media files
description: Works with the media files of a project (graphics/NAME.vcsprite, .vcpmg, .vcchar, .vcscreen, .vctiles, .vcpal; music/NAME.vcsong, .vcplay). The project folder is the current folder.

forms.summary: create a new media file from a profile

args.name: name
args.help: Name of the file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.

options.help: Profile that sets the kind and layout (sprite, character set, screen, tiles, song, palette ...).
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Creates a character set that is empty, instead of one with a reference to the default character set of the system.
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Empty character set in a subfolder
examples.cmd: vcc media new spiel --profile c64.char.hires --blank --dir graphics/fonts

notes: A new character set starts with a reference to the default character set of the system in your ROM; --blank creates it empty.
If the folder has a .vcprj, the target system of the profile must match the systems of the project.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: import sprites from SPD, raw data or another sprite asset

args.name: source
args.help: SPD file (.spd), sprite file (.vcsprite, .vcpmg) or raw data in 64-byte blocks (.bin, .prg ...).

options.help: Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Target profile (a sprite or PMG profile).
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Raw data: byte offset of the first sprite (decimal, $hex, 0xhex or %binary). For .prg, the two bytes of the load address are added.
Raw data: number of sprites; 0 means all complete blocks from the offset (at most 256).
Raw data: mode of the sprites; multicolor can be shortened to mc.
When switching to Atari PMG: number of the source sprite (0-based) that is imported.
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Raw data, five multicolor sprites
examples.cmd: vcc media import-sprite sprites.bin --name raw --offset 0 --count 5 --mode multicolor

examples.title: C64 sprite as Atari PMG
examples.cmd: vcc media import-sprite graphics/hero.vcsprite --name hero_pmg --profile atari.pmg.single --frame 0

notes: Sprite import into profiles of systems other than C64 is supported only for PMG (Atari). The output shows the path and the number of frames; notes go to stderr.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: import a song from GoatTracker, SID or a song file

args.name: source
args.help: GoatTracker song (.sng), SID file (.sid) or song file (.vcsong) of a project.

options.help: Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Target profile of the song (different chip: conversion).
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: SID file: number of the subtune (from 1); 0 takes the start song of the file.
SID file: seconds recorded from the play routine.
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Import a song for the MEGA65
examples.cmd: vcc media import-song music/tune.vcsong --name tune4 --profile mega65.sid4.song

notes: With the same chip, the song is imported (voices are padded if the target has more); otherwise it is converted. Notes go to stderr.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: convert a song to the profile of a different chip

options.help: Target profile with a different chip (e.g. atari.pokey.song).
Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: C64 song for POKEY
examples.cmd: vcc media convert music/tune.vcsong --profile atari.pokey.song --name tune_pokey

notes: If source and target have the same chip, the command stops; use `import-song` for that. Notes about the conversion (shortened envelopes, shifted octaves) go to stderr.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: import an RMT module as a POKEY song

args.name: module.rmt
args.help: RMT module (Raster Music Tracker) in the project.

options.help: Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

notes: The result always has the profile atari.pokey.song. Notes go to stderr.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

forms.summary: import a character set from a ROM image

options.help: Character set profile of the target.
Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Byte offset of the character set in the image (decimal, $hex, 0xhex or %binary).
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Second C64 character set from chargen.bin
examples.cmd: vcc media import-rom chargen.bin --profile c64.char.hires --offset 0x800 --name klein

notes: If --profile or --name is missing, the command shows on stderr what it detected (size, checksum) and lists matching profiles and offsets (exit code 2).
ROM images of original devices are protected by copyright; the copy contains the original characters. For a project that will be published, use `std-charset` (reference) instead.
The character set is saved as .vcchar in the target folder (default graphics).
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: list sources of default character sets with their status

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

notes: One line each, separated by tabs: reference, profile, system, ROM status, description.

forms.summary: add a default character set to the project as a reference or copy

args.name: ref
args.help: ROM reference of the form rom:system/role#set, e.g. rom:c64/chargen#upper.

options.help: Character set profile.
options.default_text: the profile that the list gives for the reference

options.help: Embeds the characters in the file (format 1) and writes to graphics/standard/, instead of saving only a reference.
Target folder in the project; without --copy.
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Reference to the C64 character set

notes: The file is named <system>_<set>.vcchar. Without --copy, the file contains only the reference; the original characters stay in the user's ROM. Embedded copies are not meant to be checked in or passed on.
If the ROM is missing, the file is still created; a note goes to stderr.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: import a character set from a PNG grid

args.name: grid.png
args.help: PNG with 16 characters per row in reading order (enlargement by a whole number is allowed).

options.help: Character set profile with 1 bit per pixel or MEGA65 full color.
Name of the new file without extension; letters, digits, _ and - are allowed.
Dark pixels count as set instead of light ones.
Target folder in the project (relative to the current folder).
options.default_text: default folder of the kind: music for songs, otherwise graphics

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Grid as character set
examples.cmd: vcc media import-sheet font.png --profile c64.char.hires --name font

examples.title: Dark characters on a light background
examples.cmd: vcc media import-sheet font.png --profile c64.char.hires --name font2 --invert

notes: The image must fit 16 columns and be a whole multiple of the character size (128 x 128 pixels for 256 characters of 8 x 8). Transparent pixels count as not set.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
Profile IDs (e.g. c64.char.hires, c64.sprite.multicolor, atari.pmg.single, c64.sid.song) are listed in data/profile/profiles.json.

forms.summary: write a character set as a PNG grid

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

notes: The grid has 16 characters per row, white on black, 1:1. Only character sets with 1 bit per pixel and MEGA65 full color.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

forms.summary: read a PNG image into a frame of a sprite, PMG or character set

args.name: file
args.help: Media file in the project (.vcsprite, .vcpmg or .vcchar) with embedded frames.

args.name: image.png
args.help: PNG; scaled to the frame size, pixels below 50 % opacity are transparent.

options.help: Number of the frame that is overwritten (0-based).
Video standard of the palette, pal or ntsc; only affects the Atari.
Keeps the colors of the file and rounds the image colors to them; otherwise the colors of the file are taken from the image.
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

notes: Only for profiles with at most 16 colors. If the image does not fit the available colors, the command reports a color conflict and rounds to the nearest colors; the replaced colors are shown in the output.
The file is changed in place.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

forms.summary: write a media file as assembler, binary data or BASIC DATA

options.help: Output format: asm (.byte data and .const), inc (only .const for length and, with --address, address), bin, prg (with load address, needs --address), data (BASIC DATA with @label), sbas (DATA for structured BASIC). POKEY songs: asm or rmt; PLAY songs: bas or data.
Label of the data in the source code; parts get a suffix.
options.default_text: name of the file, with - replaced by _

options.help: Load address for prg, address for inc, and for rmt the load address of the module ($hex, 0xhex or decimal).
Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Song as BASIC DATA
examples.cmd: vcc media export music/tune.vcsong --format data --label tune

notes: The files are created in build/export/; the command prints the path and size of each file. If the output has several parts (screens: chars/attrs, tiles: tiles/map/colors), each part gets its own file or section.
Media files can also be included directly with #include; this export is not needed for that.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).

forms.summary: convert old tile maps to a tile set and a screen bank

options.help: Folder of the hardware database; otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

notes: Looks in the current project folder for old tile maps (*.vctiles of kind tilemap). Files of a folder with the same tile set result in one tile set and one screen bank. The old files are removed.
The project folder is the current folder; paths to project files are relative to it. An existing target file is never overwritten (error).
